newsitem.title: UK: UK says review needed if Stagecoach wins Scotrail.
newsitem.headline: UK says review needed if Stagecoach wins Scotrail.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said on Monday that it would request a full investigation by the country's Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) if public transport operator Stagecoach Plc were to win the impending Scotrail train operating franchise.

In a statement the DTI made clear it was seeking only to anticipate one possible outcome of a process underway at the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf), in charge of the privatisation of all the country's 25 passenger rail firms.
The ministry said it understood Opraf "expects to announce the award in four to six weeks time".
Opraf has already let around 20 of the total of 25 train operating companies, mainly on seven-year franchise contracts, and Scotrail is one of several large companies left until last.

"Should the Scotrail franchise be awarded to Stagecoach, and subject to no new material considerations arising, (the DTI) will refer the merger following the public announcement of the award of the franchise agreement," the statement went on.
Stagecoach is based in the Scottish town of Perth and has always operated a range of bus services in Scotland.
According to the government statement, an acquisition of Scotrail by Stagecoach would raise concerns "relating to the supply of passenger transport services in Scotland".
Stagecoach has so far won the large southern English SouthWest Trains franchise and a far smaller contract to run trains on the Isle of Wight.
